contexts.text: The voice of weeping shall be no more heard in her () = that there shall not be evil.

(Hagar) lifted up her voice and wept () = a further degree of grief; for to lift up the voice and weep = the last [extremity] of grief, because weeping with an uplifted voice is nothing else. It is a state of the desolation of truth, and of far removal from truths, with those who are becoming spiritual, that is described in this verse.
They shall come with weeping () = their state of grief (on account of ignorance, or the desolation of truth).
Under Mourn, see this reference. AE 1164.
Esau lifted up his voice and wept () = a further state of alteration.
Purification from falsities, is signified by weeping for her father and her mother etc. ().
(Jacob) lifted up his voice and wept () = the ardour of love... For weeping belongs to sadness and also to love; and = the highest degree of both.
(The facility with which the Israelites) could break forth into bitter weeping.
(Esau and Jacob) wept () = the effect of joy on account of the conjunction of good with truths through love.
Allon-bacuth () means the oak of weeping; and an oak = the lowest of the Natural... and weeping a last farewell; from which it was customary to weep for the dead...

His father wept for him () = interior mourning; for to weep = the last extremity of grief and sorrow, thus interior mourning... Wailing and weeping over the dead was a representative external in the Ancient Churches, by which was signified interior mourning. Illustrated.
(Joseph) wept () = mercy; for to weep, when predicated of the Lord, = to have mercy, because mercy is love grieving. Illustrated.

Jerusalem over which Jesus wept () that is, which He had mercy on, and over which He grieved, = the Church, the last day of which, when there would be no charity and consequently no faith, is meant; and on this account, from His mercy and grief, He wept.
(Joseph) sought where to weep () = the effect of mercy from love.
(Joseph) littered his voice in weeping () = mercy and joy; for to weep = the effect of mercy; and also of sorrow. As it also = the effect of love, it = joy.
(Joseph) wept () = the effect of mercy; for to weep = what is from mercy, thus the effect of it.
And Benjamin wept upon his neck () = reception and thence what is reciprocal.
(Joseph) wept over them () = the effect of the affection; for to weep = the effect of mercy; here, of affection.
And (Joseph) wept long upon his neck () = mercy.
(Joseph) wept over him () = sorrow. (Explained.)
The Egyptians wept for him () = the sadness of the scientifics of the Church; for to weep = the deepest sadness, and is representative of internal mourning.
And Joseph wept when they spake unto him () = reception from love; for to weep = what is significative of both sadness and love.
Lo the child wept () = sadness.
I wept much () = grief of heart. Explained. AE 306.
Weep not () = consolation. ( = let there be no grief on that account. AE 308.)
The kings of the earth shall weep for her () = the more interior griefs of those who are in higher dominion... AR 771. AR 788. AE 1129. AE 1138. AE 1164.
See Wail.
He could not help weeping (when his Angel brother spoke to him). See AC 2304.
See Tear.

That weeping = grief of heart, is evident from the fact that weeping bursts out of the heart, and breaks out into lamentations through the mouth. And that the shedding of tears = grief of mind, is evident from the fact that it comes out from the thought through the eyes. (Continued. See Water.) This shows why it is that, in the Word, when tears are mentioned, weeping is also mentioned. Illustrated.
Lamentation because truth is destroyed, is signified by weeping (); and because good is destroyed, by wailing.
To weep between the court and the altar () = a lamentation over the vastation of Divine truth and Divine good in the Church.
Mourning because of these things, is signified by... to descend in weeping ().
